post.description: For each ref, in order (`{bucket_id, name}` as a `storage.object_ref` holds it, `{bucket, name}` for a text column marked `@storage_ref bucket=`, or `{id}` for a foreign key to `storage.objects(id)`): a signed download URL (exactly as `signObject` mints it) when the caller can read the bucket and the object (row level security on both, as the caller), the public URL instead when the bucket is public, and `null` when the caller can't read it (missing or hidden alike) or the name isn't a valid object name. All refs are read in one statement.

get.description: No key: the token is the credential. `Range` and `If-None-Match` as a download. Served sandboxed (`Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, `nosniff`); anything but an image (not SVG), video, audio, PDF or plain text is an attachment.

403.description: `token_not_valid`: another object's token, or its key was revoked

404.description: `object_not_found`: overwritten or deleted since (the signed version is no longer current; a branch reset or restore that makes it current again serves it again)

post.description: The caller must be able to read the object (row level security). The URL serves that version of the object without a key while it is the object's current version, until the URL expires or the key is revoked: an overwrite or a delete ends it (404), and re-creating the name never revives it. A branch reset or restore puts the branch back where the URL was signed, so the URL serves again until it expires, after an overwrite as after a delete; only revoking the key that minted it (or the URL expiring) ends it for good. Sign again to link to a new version.

403.description: `token_not_valid`: used already, another object's, its key was revoked or its role changed, or the app user's session ended; `not_allowed`

408.description: `request_timeout`: the body sent nothing for `CHELABASE_STORAGE_BODY_IDLE_SECS` (60 s by default)

post.description: The caller must be able to see the bucket. The URL takes one upload (`PUT`) without a key, as the caller (its role and claims): row level security decides then. Whether it may replace an existing object is fixed here (`upsert`). An app user's URL never outlives the user's session and fails once the session ends.

post.description: Parts 1 to n with none missing make the object, atomically: the total is held to the bucket's current `file_size_limit`, and the caller's policies on `storage.objects` decide again before and as the row is written. A refusal (403, 413, 415) aborts the upload.

400.description: `invalid_parts`: a gap, or a part under 5 MiB that isn't the last

403.description: `not_allowed`: the policies no longer allow it

409.description: `conflict`: the name was taken, the object changed meanwhile, or another completion of this upload won; `write_once`: an upsert over an object of a write-once bucket

put.description: Part numbers are 1 to 10000; a part is 5 MiB to 100 MiB, but the last may be smaller. Sending a part again replaces it. Its bytes are counted as they arrive and held to the bucket's `file_size_limit` less the other parts'. Part 1's first bytes must be a type the bucket allows.

413.description: `too_large`: over 100 MiB or the bucket's limit

post.description: Checks the declared `Content-Type` against the bucket's `allowed_mime_types` and the caller's INSERT (or, with `upsert`, its UPDATE) policies on `storage.objects`, then opens a session for 24 hours. Upload parts of 5 MiB to 100 MiB (the last may be smaller), then complete it. The body is empty.

BucketIdRef.description: An object by its bucket's id and its name: a `storage.object_ref` value.

BucketRef.description:
An object by its bucket's name and its name: a text column marked
`@storage_ref bucket=<bucket>` holds the name.

write_once.description:
Default false. Write-once: an object is uploaded once and never overwritten, moved,
renamed or deleted, by anyone (409 `write_once`), so its public URL is permanent. Once
true, never false again; holding objects, the bucket is neither deleted nor renamed.

IdRef.description: An object by its id: a column with a foreign key to `storage.objects(id)`.

ListObjects.description: A page of a bucket's objects.

delimiter.description: Group names by the next occurrence of it after the prefix into folders (`/`, typically).

ObjectRef.description: One object to resolve, named one of three ways.

ResolveBody.description: The refs to resolve, and the signed URLs' lifetime.

expires_in.description: A signed URL's lifetime: seconds, 1 to 604800 (7 days); default 3600.

refs.description: At most 1000, each `{bucket_id, name}`, `{bucket, name}` or `{id}`.

SignUploadBody.description: An upload URL's lifetime, and whether its upload may replace an existing object.

expires_in.description:
Seconds, 1 to 604800 (7 days); default 3600. An app user's URL never outlives the
user's session.

upsert.description:
The upload may replace an existing object (also `?upsert=true` or `x-upsert: true` on
this request). Fixed here: the uploader can't change it.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person; not stable.

sqlstate.description: The SQLSTATE of a mapped database error.

StorageErrorEnvelope.description: Every storage error: `{"error": {...}}`, the data API's envelope.

UpdateBucket.description: A bucket's changes; a field left out stays as it is.

name.description: A new name (not of a write-once bucket holding objects).

write_once.description: Turned on at any time, never off again (409 `write_once`).

bearer.description: A data API key (`chk_pub_…` or `chk_sec_…`) as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`
